newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Kinnock calls for trucker compensation.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock calls for trucker compensation.

text.p: European Union transport chief Neil Kinnock called on Thursday for compensation for lorry drivers caught by French fishermen's latest protest and accused the French of not paying up for last year's truck strikes.

Kinnock's spokeswoman, speaking after news that fishermen had suspended blockades of French ports Dunkirk, Calais and Boulogne, told a news conference the Commissioner had written to to French Transport Minister Bernard Pons.

"We sent a letter to Mr Pons... pointing out the disastrous effect this was having on road haulage and underlining the commitment of the French to compensate truckers," spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said.
She confirmed that Kinnock knew of British truckers' claims that they had not received compensation as promised after an unrelated French hauliers' strike last year.
"It is indeed our understanding that some hauliers still have not been compensated for the last time and we drew French attention to this. We hope that they will get on the case."
Kinnock mentioned the issue in his letter, released to reporters, speaking of the "extreme slowness" with which only a very few claims had been met.
He asked Pons for a report on how many claims had been submitted, the stage they had reached and how much had been paid to affected drivers from France's neighbouring countries.

Meanwhile, near the British port of Dover, up to 400 truck drivers stranded on the motorway prepared to move their vehicles after striking French fishermen suspended their blockade of selected Channel ports.
The 18-mile (29 km) long traffic jam began on Tuesday after the French fishermen began their protest over European Union regulations on net sizes.
